title: TuringQ Planning to IPO and In Race to Become China’s First Public Quantum Firm - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Shanghai photonic quantum firm TuringQ has begun pre-IPO tutoring with the Shanghai branch of the CSRC, advised by Guotai Haitong Securities, in a race with Origin Quantum, Ciqtek and QBoson to become China's first listed quantum computing company. TuringQ raised nearly 1 billion yuan ($148M) in 2026 with an April Series C valuing it above 7 billion yuan ($1.04B), and its differentiator is photonic architecture plus a Wuxi pilot line producing thin-film lithium niobate photonic chips at wafer scale.

insights.claim: TuringQ has initiated pre-IPO tutoring with the Shanghai branch of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, advised by Guotai Haitong Securities, aiming to become China's first publicly listed quantum computing company.
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: A Chinese quantum listing would create the first public comparable outside the U.S. cohort, giving global investors a new valuation anchor for the sector.
insights.locator: Opening paragraph — "Shanghai-based photonic quantum firm TuringQ"

insights.claim: TuringQ is competing against a crowded domestic pipeline including Origin Quantum, Ciqtek and QBoson, all of which have advanced through listing tutoring or application stages over the past year.
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: Multiple simultaneous quantum IPO candidates mean a wave of Chinese listings, not one event — expect comparative pricing pressure.
insights.locator: "TuringQ joins a crowded pipeline of domestic peers"

insights.claim: In April 2026 the Shanghai Stock Exchange explicitly designated quantum technology a strategic emerging industry under its STAR Market listing rules, creating a clearer path for quantum startups to go public.
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: Regulatory designation is the proximate cause of the listing rush — policy, not technical readiness, is setting the IPO timetable.
insights.quote: In April 2026, the Shanghai Stock Exchange explicitly designated quantum technology as a strategic emerging industry under its STAR Market listing rules, providing quantum startups with a clearer framework for going public.
insights.locator: "The listing ambition comes amid broader structural support"

insights.claim: The Chinese quantum ecosystem is transitioning from early-stage venture funding toward commercialization via public capital markets, part of a broader rush among Chinese hard-tech enterprises to list.
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: Public-market funding gives Chinese quantum firms durable capital for capital-intensive R&D, narrowing a financing gap versus U.S. peers.
insights.locator: Opening paragraph — "the move reflects both a broader rush"

insights.claim: TuringQ, founded in February 2021 by legal representative Jin Xianmin and controlled by Shanghai Siliang Quantum Technology, focuses on photonic quantum architectures rather than the more common superconducting or trapped-ion routes.
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: A photonics-only national champion diversifies China's architecture exposure away from the superconducting path dominant in the West.
insights.locator: "Founded in February 2021 by legal representative Jin Xianmin"

insights.claim: The stated advantages of the photonic approach are room-temperature operation, high scalability, and direct compatibility with existing optical communications infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: Room-temperature operation removes the cryogenic cost stack that burdens superconducting rivals — the core economic argument for photonics.

insights.claim: TuringQ's pilot production facility in Wuxi, Jiangsu Province began operating in June 2025 to produce thin-film lithium niobate photonic chips, enabling wafer-scale manufacturing with thousands of optical components on a single chip.
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: Owning a wafer-scale TFLN line is a manufacturing moat that also serves classical photonics markets — the strongest asset backing the IPO story.
insights.locator: "The company’s commercialization efforts reached a significant milestone in June 2025"

insights.claim: TuringQ secured nearly 1 billion yuan ($148 million USD) during 2026 alone, with an April Series C round pushing its valuation past 7 billion yuan ($1.04 billion USD).
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: A ~$1B private mark sets the floor expectation for the IPO price and a reference point for valuing unlisted photonic quantum peers.

insights.claim: TuringQ has earmarked its new capital for advancing practical photonic quantum computers, cultivating a quantum algorithm ecosystem, and expanding quantum-powered intelligent computing infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: Spending on an algorithm ecosystem alongside hardware suggests a platform strategy rather than pure component sales.

insights.claim: Industry analysts caution that early listings do not guarantee technological maturity, even though "first quantum stock" status carries symbolic weight and supplies long-term liquidity for capital-intensive R&D.
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: Treat first-mover listing status as a liquidity event, not technical validation — the risk is paying a scarcity premium for unproven capability.
insights.quote: while attaining “first quantum stock” status carries strong symbolic weight and provides much-needed long-term liquidity for capital-intensive R&D, early listings do not guarantee technological maturity

insights.claim: Specialized hardware sales and cloud-based services remain the primary near-term revenue drivers for Chinese quantum firms, with industrial viability ultimately resting on whether enterprise customers will adopt and pay for quantum applications at scale.
insights.speaker: Quantum Computing Report
insights.so_what: Enterprise willingness to pay is the single variable that decides the sector — monitor commercial revenue mix in post-IPO disclosures.
insights.locator: "Specialized hardware sales and cloud-based services remain"
